agent.result_text:
I've made the change. The main test (`deferred bound counts`) now passes; it failed before. The other three scenarios still fail, at exactly the same lines as before my change, on steps that have nothing to do with deferral.

**What changed.** Being "deferred" now also requires the claim not to be bound by a statement. The rule is the same in two places, one on the server and one on the screen:
- `Claim.isDeferredOn` in `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/claim/Claim.java`
- `deferred()` in `src/main/frontend/src/app/core/claims.ts`

Everything else that checks deferral calls one of these two: the totals, counts, overdue, the late charge, settle and split refusals, statements and periods. So while a claim is bound and deferred:
- it stays in the totals and counts, and can be settled;
- a new statement that still counts it keeps it bound;
- once the binding ends (the statement is cancelled, or the next statement leaves it unbound), the deferral takes effect until its date.

**One behaviour change.** The "is it OPEN?" check is gone. The test expects a claim settled while bound to show as deferred, and drop out of the totals, once it's unbound. It also expects a VOID claim to show as deferred. A side effect: a claim deferred, then settled after its deferral date passed, would show as deferred again if the sheet's date were moved back before that date. This rarely matters.

**Why the other three scenarios still fail.** These tests have expectations the app can't meet, and I'm not allowed to edit the test:
- **Scenarios 2 and 3** (spec lines 909 and 1559) expect the parent sheet to read the literal text `__SHEET__-p`. The test sets the parent to the real id, `${sheet}-p`, and the screen shows that. It looks like a placeholder that was never filled in when the test was written.
- **Scenario 1** (spec line 248) sets a flag that runs until 2026-03-12, on a sheet whose date is already 2026-04-07. A flag only shows while it's in force, so nothing appears and the step times out. Later the same test expects the flag to show as empty (line 500), which is how the app already behaves.

Someone who can edit the spec will need to fix those three tests; I don't think any change to the app would make them pass.
